ts.gate.safety_stops.title: Before we start: is any of this happening now?
ts.gate.safety_stops.body:
Answer from what you can see, hear, or smell right now. Don’t take the thermostat off the wall or open any equipment to check.

Thermostat steps come only after this check.

options.label: A carbon monoxide (CO) alarm is sounding
options.fact: CO alarm reported at the thermostat check.

options.label: I smell gas (like rotten eggs) or hear hissing
options.hint: Leave first. Don’t use switches inside.
options.fact: Gas smell or hissing reported at the thermostat check.

options.label: Burning or electrical smell, smoke, or scorched or melted wires at the thermostat
options.hint: Don’t touch the thermostat or its wires.
options.fact: Burning smell, smoke, or scorched thermostat wires reported.

options.label: A breaker for the heating or cooling keeps tripping
options.fact: Breaker for the HVAC keeps tripping.

options.label: Water pooling at or around the furnace or indoor unit
options.hint: Don’t open the unit or clear the drain.
options.fact: Water at the furnace or indoor unit reported.

options.label: The thermostat runs baseboard or wall heaters, or is marked 120 V or 240 V
options.fact: Line-voltage (120/240 V) thermostat reported.

options.label: Someone told me to open the furnace, air handler, or outdoor unit, or to change thermostat wires
options.fact: Fix would need opening HVAC equipment or changing wires.

options.label: None of these
options.fact: Thermostat safety check: none of the stops reported.

options.label: New hazard now (burning smell, smoke, sparks, gas smell, CO alarm, or water at electrical parts)
options.fact: New hazard reported during the thermostat check.

ts.settings.mode_setpoint.title: Check the mode and temperature
ts.settings.mode_setpoint.body:
1. Set the mode to Heat for heat, or Cool for cooling. In Off, nothing runs.
2. Set the temperature at least 3°F above the room for Heat, or at least 3°F below the room for Cool.
3. Wait 5 minutes. Many systems wait a few minutes to protect the equipment, and changing the setting again starts that wait over.

{step panel: MODE}

options.label: I changed the mode or temperature, and now it’s working
options.fact: User set the mode and temperature, and heating or cooling started.

options.label: The screen says it’s heating or cooling, but nothing runs after 5 minutes
options.fact: User set the mode and temperature. The thermostat showed a call, but nothing ran after 5 minutes.

options.label: The mode I need (like Auto or emergency heat) isn’t offered
options.fact: Needed mode not offered on the thermostat.

options.label: It heats in Cool, or cools in Heat
options.fact: Heating and cooling appear reversed.

options.label: It won’t let me change the setting (locked or limited)
options.fact: Thermostat setting locked or limited.

My screen looks different

options.fact: Thermostat screen did not match the guide.

ts.settings.hold_schedule.title: Check for a hold or a schedule
ts.settings.hold_schedule.body:
A change you make by hand often lasts only until the next scheduled time. Some thermostats can also hold it until you cancel it. If the temperature seems to change by itself, a schedule or a hold is the usual reason.

1. Look for a hold message on the main screen.
2. Cancel the hold to go back to the schedule, or keep it if that’s what you want.
3. If the schedule itself is wrong, fix it on the thermostat or in its app.

{step panel: HOLD}

options.label: I cancelled or set the hold, and it’s behaving now
options.fact: User cancelled or set a hold, or fixed the schedule.

ts.settings.fan.title: Check the fan setting
ts.settings.fan.body:
Auto runs the fan only while heating or cooling. On runs it all the time. Some thermostats also have Circulate, or a minimum fan time each hour, which runs it between cycles.

1. Set the fan to Auto.
2. Stop any fan timer or fan schedule.
3. If your thermostat has a minimum fan time, turn it down to zero.

{step panel: FAN}

ts.settings.em_aux_heat.title: Check emergency and backup heat
ts.settings.em_aux_heat.body:
Emergency heat runs only the backup heat, and it costs more to run. It stays on until someone switches it off.

1. Switch the mode from emergency heat back to Heat.
2. Avoid big jumps in the temperature setting. They can bring on the backup heat.

ts.power.blank_screen.title: Blank screen: checks from the floor
ts.power.blank_screen.body:
First: any burning smell, smoke, or scorched wires? Choose the last option.

1. If your thermostat takes batteries, put in fresh ones (steps below).
2. Check that the furnace or air-handler door is fully closed. Look only. Some systems shut off when the door isn’t seated.
3. Check that the furnace power switch is on. It often looks like a light switch on or near the furnace.
4. Notice whether other equipment has power: the furnace or air-handler light, the outdoor unit, or lights on the same part of the house. Just look. Don’t touch anything.
5. Don’t reset breakers in this check. If a breaker for the heating or cooling looks tripped, choose that option.

{step panel: POWER}

ts_co_gas_now.title: Gas or carbon monoxide ends this check.
ts_co_gas_now.explanation: Stop. This isn’t something to troubleshoot here. If you smell gas, a CO alarm is sounding, or you smell burning or see smoke: leave the home and call 911 or your gas utility from outside. For wiring or electrical problems, turn the system off at the thermostat and call a licensed professional.
actions: If you smell gas or a carbon monoxide alarm is sounding, leave the building and call for help from outside. Do not operate switches inside.
Do not return to troubleshooting until the hazard has been handled.
ts_co_gas_now.avoid: Do not change thermostat settings, open covers, or go back inside to check.

ts_burning_electrical.title: A burning smell or damaged wires end this check.
ts_burning_electrical.explanation: Stop. This isn’t something to troubleshoot here. If you smell gas, a CO alarm is sounding, or you smell burning or see smoke: leave the home and call 911 or your gas utility from outside. For wiring or electrical problems, turn the system off at the thermostat and call a licensed professional.
actions: If there is smoke, fire, or sparks, get people away and call 911 from safety.
If there is no smoke or fire, call a licensed HVAC professional or electrician.
Do not return to troubleshooting until the hazard has been handled.
ts_burning_electrical.avoid: Do not touch, pull off, or rewire the thermostat, and do not reset breakers to test it.

ts_breaker_retrip.title: Don’t reset that breaker.
ts_breaker_retrip.explanation: A breaker that keeps tripping can mean an electrical fault, so this is a job for a professional.
actions: Leave that breaker as it is and call a licensed HVAC professional or electrician.
Tell the pro which breaker tripped and when.
If you smell burning or see smoke, get people away and call 911 from safety.
ts_breaker_retrip.avoid: Don’t reset the breaker, open the electrical panel, or open the furnace or outdoor unit.

ts_water_indoor_unit.title: Water at the indoor unit is a job for a pro.
ts_water_indoor_unit.explanation: Water around the furnace or indoor unit, especially with a cooling-failure code, often means the drain is blocked or a safety switch shut the cooling off. Clearing it means opening the unit, which is work for a pro.
actions: Set the thermostat to Off.
If water is near an outlet, cord, or anything electrical, stay clear. Shut power only from a dry place you already know.
Call a licensed HVAC professional. Tell them any code the thermostat shows.
ts_water_indoor_unit.avoid: Don’t open the unit, clear the drain, or reset any safety switch.

ts_line_voltage_stop.title: High-voltage thermostats aren’t covered.
ts_line_voltage_stop.explanation: Thermostats for baseboard or wall heaters often run on 120 or 240 volts. They should only be installed or removed by a licensed professional.
actions: Leave the thermostat on the wall.
Call a licensed electrician or HVAC professional.
ts_line_voltage_stop.avoid: Don’t take the thermostat off the wall or touch its wires.

ts_open_cabinet_stop.title: This check never opens equipment or changes wires.
ts_open_cabinet_stop.explanation: The furnace, air handler, and outdoor unit hold high voltage and moving parts. A C wire, power adapter, or kit means work inside them, which is for a professional.
actions: Leave every cover on.
Call a licensed HVAC professional. Tell them your thermostat model and what you were told to do.
ts_open_cabinet_stop.avoid: Don’t open the furnace, air handler, or outdoor unit, and don’t add, move, or swap thermostat wires.

ts_hazard_now.title: A new hazard ends this check.
ts_hazard_now.explanation: Stop. This isn’t something to troubleshoot here. If you smell gas, a CO alarm is sounding, or you smell burning or see smoke: leave the home and call 911 or your gas utility from outside. For wiring or electrical problems, turn the system off at the thermostat and call a licensed professional.
actions: If you smell gas or a carbon monoxide alarm is sounding, leave the building and call for help from outside. Do not operate switches inside.
If there is smoke, fire, or sparks, get people away and call 911 from safety.
If water is at electrical equipment, stay clear. Shut power only from a dry place you already know.
Do not return to troubleshooting until the hazard has been handled.
ts_hazard_now.avoid: Do not keep diagnosing, open covers, or touch wet equipment.

ts_mode_fixed_basic.title: A setting was the problem.
ts_mode_fixed_basic.explanation: The right mode and a target on the right side of the room temperature let the system run.
actions: Leave it in Heat or Cool for the season.
If it stops again with the right settings, start a new check.
If the screen shows it’s heating or cooling and nothing runs, call a licensed HVAC professional.
ts_mode_fixed_basic.avoid: Don’t change installer or equipment settings.

ts_hold_fixed_basic.title: A hold or the schedule was the cause.
ts_hold_fixed_basic.explanation: A change made by hand can hold the temperature until the next scheduled time, or until someone cancels it.
actions: Pick the hold that fits: until the next scheduled time, or until you cancel it.
If the temperature still changes when no one touched it, features like Eco, Away, or learning schedules may be on. Those aren’t covered in this first version.
ts_hold_fixed_basic.avoid: Don’t change installer or equipment settings.

ts_fan_fixed_basic.urgency: Fan set the way you want
ts_fan_fixed_basic.title: A fan setting was the cause.
ts_fan_fixed_basic.explanation: Auto runs the fan only during heating or cooling. On, Circulate, and a minimum fan time each hour run it more.
actions: Leave the fan on Auto unless you want extra air movement.
If the fan runs with Auto set and no heating or cooling, call a licensed HVAC professional.
ts_fan_fixed_basic.avoid: Don’t open the furnace or air handler.

ts_wifi_fixed_basic.title: The thermostat is connected again.
ts_wifi_fixed_basic.explanation: New routers, new passwords, and 5 GHz-only networks are common causes.
actions: If you change your router or password again, repeat the Wi-Fi steps.
If it keeps dropping, especially in very hot or cold weather, it may not be getting steady power. A licensed HVAC professional can check that.
ts_wifi_fixed_basic.avoid: Don’t change thermostat wires or installer settings to fix Wi-Fi.

ts_eheat_off_basic.title: Emergency heat was left on.
ts_eheat_off_basic.explanation: Emergency heat runs only the backup heat and costs more. It stays on until someone switches it off.
actions: Leave the mode on Heat.
Use emergency heat only when the heat pump can’t run. If you need it often, call a licensed HVAC professional.
ts_eheat_off_basic.avoid: Don’t change backup-heat lockout, balance point, or threshold settings.

ts_wait_cleared_basic.title: The wait was normal.
ts_wait_cleared_basic.explanation: Many systems wait about 5 minutes before starting again, to protect the equipment.
actions: Change the setting once, then give it 5 minutes.
If the wait lasts longer than 5 minutes or happens every time, call a licensed HVAC professional.
ts_wait_cleared_basic.avoid: Don’t turn off or shorten the compressor protection.

ts_battery_fixed_basic.title: Low batteries were the cause.
ts_battery_fixed_basic.explanation: Fresh alkaline batteries clear most low-battery warnings.
actions: Replace them about once a year, and before a long trip.
Check the time and schedule afterward. Some models lose the clock if the swap takes too long.
ts_battery_fixed_basic.avoid: Don’t disconnect thermostat wires to reach the batteries.

ts_power_restored_basic.title: The screen is on again.
ts_power_restored_basic.explanation: Dead batteries, a furnace power switch left off, or a furnace door that isn’t fully closed can blank the screen.
actions: If the screen goes blank again, start a new check.
If a breaker for the heating or cooling trips, leave it as it is and call a licensed professional.
ts_power_restored_basic.avoid: Don’t reset breakers, and don’t remove the furnace door.

ts_calling_no_run.title: The thermostat is asking, but the system isn’t answering.
ts_calling_no_run.explanation: If the screen shows it’s heating or cooling and nothing runs after a few minutes, the cause is usually in the equipment or wiring, which is work for a pro.
actions: Call a licensed HVAC professional. Tell them your thermostat model, the mode and setting, and what the screen shows.
If you smell burning or see smoke, get people away and call 911 from safety.
ts_calling_no_run.avoid: Don’t open the furnace or outdoor unit, change wires, or reset breakers to test it.

ts_power_breaker_pro.title: A tripped breaker or missing power is a job for a pro.
ts_power_breaker_pro.explanation: This check doesn’t include resetting breakers. A tripped breaker, or no power to the heating and cooling equipment, can have an electrical cause that a licensed HVAC professional or electrician should find.
actions: Leave the breaker as it is and call a licensed HVAC professional or electrician.
Tell the pro what you saw: which breaker looked tripped, or which equipment and lights had no power.
If you smell burning or see smoke, get people away and call 911 from safety.
ts_power_breaker_pro.avoid: Don’t reset breakers, open the electrical panel, or open the furnace or outdoor unit.

ts_blank_after_basics.title: The thermostat still isn’t getting steady power.
ts_blank_after_basics.explanation: When the batteries and switches check out, the usual causes are a loose or missing power wire or a problem at the furnace controls. A pro checks those.
actions: Call a licensed HVAC professional. Tell them your model and any code or light you saw.
Nest owners: Google may offer a power adapter for some low-power codes. If it goes inside the furnace, let the pro fit it.
ts_blank_after_basics.avoid: Don’t pull wires, move the R or Rc slider, or add a C wire yourself.

ts_wait_persists.title: The wait doesn’t end.
ts_wait_persists.explanation: A wait that lasts past 5 minutes, or comes back every time, can mean a power drop, a wiring fault, or an equipment problem that a pro should check.
actions: Call a licensed HVAC professional. Tell them what the screen shows and how long it lasts.
ts_wait_persists.avoid: Don’t turn off or shorten the compressor protection.

ts_fan_problem_pro.title: The fan isn’t following the thermostat.
ts_fan_problem_pro.explanation: If the fan runs with the thermostat on Auto and no heating or cooling, or won’t run at all, a relay or control board may be at fault, which a pro checks.
actions: Call a licensed HVAC professional. Tell them the fan setting and what the fan does.
ts_fan_problem_pro.avoid: Don’t open the furnace or air handler to look.

ts_aux_persistent.title: Backup heat is doing too much of the work.
ts_aux_persistent.explanation: If backup heat runs a lot in normal Heat mode, the thermostat shows HEAT PUMP FAILURE, or the outdoor unit isn’t running, the heat pump may need service.
actions: Call a licensed HVAC professional. Tell them what the thermostat shows and whether the outdoor unit runs.
Use emergency heat only if the house is getting too cold, and tell the pro you did.
ts_aux_persistent.avoid: Don’t change backup-heat lockout, balance point, or threshold settings.

ts_code_to_pro.urgency: Give the code to a pro
ts_code_to_pro.title: Write the code down for your HVAC pro.
ts_code_to_pro.explanation: Apart from Wi-Fi, low-battery, and wait messages, this check doesn’t interpret codes.
actions: Write down the exact code or message, your thermostat model, and what the system was doing.
Call a licensed HVAC professional. If the message names the thermostat itself, like MEMORY ERROR, the thermostat may need replacing.
ts_code_to_pro.avoid: Don’t clear the code to test, open equipment, or change installer settings.

ts_installer_guard.title: Don’t change it.
ts_installer_guard.explanation: This setting is for installers. Changing it can damage your equipment or leave you without heat or cooling. Don’t change it. Note what it says and share it with your HVAC professional.
actions: Back out of that screen without saving.
Call a licensed HVAC professional if heating or cooling still isn’t right.
ts_installer_guard.avoid: Don’t change equipment type, heat pump, staging, backup-heat, threshold, compressor-protection, or wiring settings.

ts_heat_cool_reversed.title: Heating and cooling look reversed.
ts_heat_cool_reversed.explanation: When a heat pump heats on a cooling call, or cools on a heating call, the cause is almost always an installer setting or the wiring, which a pro sets.
actions: Set the thermostat to Off.
Call a licensed HVAC professional or the installer. Tell them when it started, especially if a new thermostat was just put in.
ts_heat_cool_reversed.avoid: Don’t change the reversing valve (O/B) or equipment settings yourself, even if an app shows how.

ts_wifi_device_fault.title: This looks like a thermostat fault, not a setting.
ts_wifi_device_fault.explanation: Some Wi-Fi errors that stay after a restart, like Nest W5 or Honeywell WIFI MODULE ERROR, mean the thermostat may need repair or replacement.
actions: Contact the thermostat maker’s support. Have your model and the exact message ready.
Heating and cooling may still run from the thermostat itself while it’s offline.
ts_wifi_device_fault.avoid: Don’t open the thermostat or change installer settings.

ts_advanced_off.title: Capacitor, contactor, and board work are not offered in the thermostat check.
ts_advanced_off.explanation: Advanced electrical stays off for this check.
actions: Leave covers on.
Call a licensed HVAC professional. Tell them what the system was doing and that you did not remove covers.
ts_advanced_off.avoid: Do not start a capacitor, contactor, or board repair from this thermostat check.

ts_brand_not_covered.title: This first check covers Google Nest, Honeywell Home, ecobee, and Amazon thermostats.
ts_brand_not_covered.explanation: Other brands come in a later version. This check won’t guess at their menus.
actions: Use your thermostat’s manual or the maker’s help pages.
If heating or cooling isn’t working after the basic settings, call a licensed HVAC professional.
If your system has a Carrier, Trane, or Lennox wall control, read the alert and call your dealer.
ts_brand_not_covered.avoid: Don’t change installer or equipment settings.

ts_model_not_in_v0.title: This model isn’t in the first version.
ts_model_not_in_v0.explanation: We only show steps for models we’ve checked against the maker’s manual.
actions: Use your model’s manual or the maker’s help pages.
If a step leads into an installer or equipment menu, stop and call a licensed HVAC professional.
ts_model_not_in_v0.avoid: Don’t change installer or equipment settings.

ts_model_unconfirmed.title: Steps depend on the exact model.
ts_model_unconfirmed.explanation: Menus differ between models, so guessing can send you down the wrong steps.
actions: Look for the model name on the box, the receipt, or in the maker’s app.
Start again when you know it.
ts_model_unconfirmed.avoid: Don’t pull the thermostat off the wall or open it to find the model.

ts_landing_not_in_v0.title: This first check covers the most common settings problems.
ts_landing_not_in_v0.explanation: Eco and Away features, learning schedules, remote sensors, temperature readings, short cycling, humidity settings, and app support come in a later version.
actions: Check the maker’s help pages for that feature.
If heating or cooling isn’t working, call a licensed HVAC professional and tell them what you noticed.
ts_landing_not_in_v0.avoid: Don’t change installer or equipment settings.

ts_screen_different.title: Your screen doesn’t match.
ts_screen_different.explanation: Thanks. Stop here and don’t keep pressing through menus. Your device may have a newer layout. Check [Brand]’s official help page ([link]) or contact a licensed HVAC professional. We’ll review this step.
actions: Write down what your screen shows and your thermostat model.
If heating or cooling isn’t working, call a licensed HVAC professional.
ts_screen_different.avoid: Don’t keep pressing through menus to find a match.

ts_settings_unsure.title: The next steps depend on what the thermostat shows.
ts_settings_unsure.explanation: If you can’t tell the mode or setting, the manual or the maker’s app can show it.
actions: Look at the thermostat or its app in good light, and note the mode, the setting, and any message.
Start again when you can see them. If you can’t, call a licensed HVAC professional.
ts_settings_unsure.avoid: Don’t open the thermostat to look for settings.

ts_locked_or_limited.title: The thermostat may be locked or limited.
ts_locked_or_limited.explanation: Screen locks, temperature limits, and landlord or installer passwords can stop changes.
actions: Check your manual for the screen lock or temperature limits.
If a landlord or installer set a password, ask them.
ts_locked_or_limited.avoid: Don’t try to get around a password or open the thermostat.

NEST-LT3.label: Nest Learning Thermostat, 3rd gen or older

ECB-PRM.label: ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium or Enhanced

NEST-LT4.text: Press the display to open the menu. Turn the ring to the mode item and press. Turn to Heat or Cool and press again. You can also change the mode in the Google Home app.

NEST-NT.text: Tap the touch strip to open the menu. Slide to the temperature mode item and tap. Slide to Heat or Cool and tap. You can also use the Google Home app.

NEST-LT3.text: Press the ring to open the menu. Turn to the mode item and press. Pick Heat or Cool, press, then confirm.

NEST-E.text: Press the ring to open the quick menu. Turn to the mode you want and press.

HW-T5.text: Press the mode button on the home screen and pick Heat or Cool. Auto and emergency heat show only if the installer set them up.

HW-T9.text: Tap the screen to wake it and open the menu at the bottom. Choose the system mode item, pick Heat or Cool, then tap Done.

ECB-PRM.text: Tap the mode symbol above the temperature, or open the menu and find the system mode setting. Pick Heat or Cool.

ECB-ESS.text: Set the mode to Heat or Cool, set the temperature at least 3°F past the room temperature, and wait 5 minutes.

HW-FP6.text: Press System. Each press moves to the next mode. Stop when the display shows Heat or Cool. Auto and Em Heat show only on some setups. If the mode you need isn’t there, an installer has to turn it on.

HW-X2P.text: Press the mode button until Heat or Cool shows. The modes you see depend on how it was set up.

AMZ-AST.text: Press the center button to step through the modes. The screen uses symbols, not words: heating shows in red and cooling in blue. Or, in the Alexa app, open your thermostat and use the mode button under the dial.

NEST-LT4.text: In the Google Home app, open the thermostat’s schedules. Heat, Cool, and Heat • Cool each keep their own schedule, so check the one for the mode you’re using. Learning schedules can be turned off in the thermostat’s settings.

NEST-NT.text: In the Google Home app, open the thermostat’s schedules. Heat, Cool, and Heat • Cool each keep their own schedule, so check the one for the mode you’re using. Learning schedules can be turned off in the thermostat’s settings.

NEST-LT3.text: In the Google Home app, open the thermostat’s schedules. Heat, Cool, and Heat • Cool each keep their own schedule, so check the one for the mode you’re using. Learning schedules can be turned off in the thermostat’s settings.

NEST-E.text: In the Google Home app, open the thermostat’s schedules. Heat, Cool, and Heat • Cool each keep their own schedule, so check the one for the mode you’re using. Learning schedules can be turned off in the thermostat’s settings.

HW-T5.text: After you change the temperature, the screen shows how long the change will hold. Touch that to go back to the schedule or to hold it permanently.

ECB-PRM.text: A change made by hand shows a bar with an end time and an X. Tap the X to cancel the hold and go back to the schedule. You can also cancel it in the ecobee app.

ECB-ESS.text: Look for a hold or a schedule on the thermostat or in its app, and cancel a hold you don’t want.

HW-FP6.text: Temporary on the display means a change made with the arrows. It ends at the next scheduled time. Hold means the temperature stays put until you cancel it. To go back to your schedule from either one, press Run Schedule.

HW-X2P.text: Using the arrows alone holds the change until the next scheduled time. To end any hold, press the hold button until the cancel option shows.

AMZ-AST.text: A change made by hand lasts until the next scheduled change. To check the schedule, open the thermostat in the Alexa app, go to its device settings, then its schedules, and make sure the thermostat schedule is switched on.

NEST-LT4.text: In the Google Home app, check the thermostat’s fan: a fan timer or a fan schedule can keep it running. Stop the timer or turn the schedule off.

NEST-NT.text: In the Google Home app, check the thermostat’s fan: a fan timer or a fan schedule can keep it running. Stop the timer or turn the schedule off.

NEST-LT3.text: In the Google Home app, check the thermostat’s fan: a fan timer or a fan schedule can keep it running. Stop the timer or turn the schedule off.

NEST-E.text: In the Google Home app, check the thermostat’s fan: a fan timer or a fan schedule can keep it running. Stop the timer or turn the schedule off.

HW-T5.text: Press the fan button and pick Auto.

HW-T9.text: Open the menu, choose Fan, and pick Auto. Circulate runs the fan about a third of the time.

ECB-ESS.text: Set the fan to Auto unless you want it to run more, and clear any fan timer.

HW-FP6.text: Press Fan until the display shows Auto. Auto runs the fan only while heating or cooling. On runs the fan all the time.

HW-X2P.text: Press the fan button until Auto shows. Circulate runs the fan about a third of the time.

AMZ-AST.text: Fan is one of the modes the center button steps through. If the thermostat is in Fan mode, step on to Heat, Cool, or Auto.

NEST-LT4.text: Restart the thermostat from its settings menu (choose Restart; your settings stay). Then open the network setting and choose your network. Don’t pick Factory Reset.

NEST-NT.text: Restart the thermostat from its settings menu (choose Restart; your settings stay). Then open the network setting and choose your network. Don’t pick Factory Reset.

NEST-LT3.text: Restart the thermostat: in settings, open Reset and choose Restart only. Don’t choose any other reset option. Then open the network setting and choose your network.

NEST-E.text: Restart the thermostat: in settings, open Reset and choose Restart only. Don’t choose any other reset option. Then open the network setting and choose your network.

HW-T5.text: Restart: gently pull the thermostat straight off its wall plate, wait about 30 seconds, and press it back on. Don’t touch the wires behind it. Then reconnect Wi-Fi using the Wi-Fi reset option or the Resideo app. Pick only the Wi-Fi reset. It needs a 2.4 GHz network.

HW-T6.text: Restart: gently pull the thermostat straight off its wall plate, wait about 30 seconds, and press it back on. Don’t touch the wires behind it. Then reconnect Wi-Fi using the Wi-Fi reset option or the Resideo app. Pick only the Wi-Fi reset. It needs a 2.4 GHz network.

ECB-PRM.text: Open the menu, go to Settings, then Wi-Fi. Make sure Wi-Fi is on, pick your 2.4 GHz network, and enter the password.

ECB-ESS.text: Open the menu, go to Settings, then Wi-Fi, and pick your network.

AMZ-AST.text: Restart: gently pull the faceplate off, wait a moment, and push it back on. Then, in the Alexa app, open the thermostat’s device settings, then its configuration, then Wi-Fi. Use only the Wi-Fi item there. It needs a 2.4 GHz network. Code 3:16:0:1 means a weak signal; 3:5:0:1 means the router has no internet.

NEST-LT4.text: In the Google Home app, open the thermostat’s settings and turn Emergency Heat off. Don’t change the equipment or heat pump settings.

NEST-NT.text: In the Google Home app, open the thermostat’s settings and turn Emergency Heat off. Don’t change the equipment or heat pump settings.

NEST-LT3.text: In the Google Home app, open the thermostat’s settings and turn Emergency Heat off. Don’t change the equipment or heat pump settings.

NEST-E.text: In the Google Home app, open the thermostat’s settings and turn Emergency Heat off. Don’t change the equipment or heat pump settings.

HW-T5.text: Press the mode button and pick Heat instead of emergency heat.

HW-T9.text: Open the menu, choose the system mode item, pick Heat instead of Em Heat, then tap Done.

ECB-PRM.text: Switch the system mode from Aux to Heat. If a pop-up offers to change outdoor-temperature settings, don’t change them. Taking the short override it offers is fine.

ECB-ESS.text: If emergency heat is on, switch the mode back to Heat. Don’t change installer settings.

HW-FP6.text: Em Heat on the display means only the backup heat is running, and it costs more. Press System until the display shows Heat to go back to normal heat.

HW-X2P.text: Press the mode button until Heat shows instead of emergency heat.

AMZ-AST.text: In the Alexa app, open the thermostat’s device settings, then its configuration, and switch Emergency Heat off. Use only the Emergency Heat item there. A flashing yellow status light can mean emergency or backup heat is running.

HW-FP6.text: Cool On flashing (or Heat On on a heat pump) means the thermostat is waiting a few minutes to protect the equipment. It stops flashing once the system runs. Give it about 5 minutes and don’t keep changing the setting.

HW-T6.text: Cool On or Heat On flashing means the protection wait. Give it about 5 minutes.

AMZ-AST.text: A flashing yellow status light can mean the system is in its protection wait. Allow 5 to 7 minutes.

HW-T5.text: Make one change, then wait 5 minutes. A wait of about 5 minutes is normal.

ECB-ESS.text: Make one change, then wait 5 minutes. A wait of about 5 minutes is normal.

NEST-NT.text: This model runs on two AAA batteries. Pull the display straight off its base, put in fresh alkaline AAA batteries, and press it back on.

NEST-LT4.text: A blinking red light means the battery is very low. No light at all can mean it isn’t getting enough power from the system. If either comes back, a pro checks the power.

NEST-LT3.text: A blinking red light means the battery is very low. No light at all can mean it isn’t getting enough power from the system. If either comes back, a pro checks the power.

NEST-E.text: A blinking red light means the battery is very low. No light at all can mean it isn’t getting enough power from the system. If either comes back, a pro checks the power.

HW-T5.text: These models have no batteries. They get their power from the heating and cooling system.

HW-T9.text: These models have no batteries. They get their power from the heating and cooling system.

HW-T6.text: Some T6 Pro models take AA batteries. If yours does, put in fresh alkaline AA batteries.

ECB-PRM.text: ecobee thermostats need steady power from the system. A calibrating message for up to about 20 minutes after power returns is normal. If it keeps restarting, that’s a power problem for a pro.

ECB-ESS.text: ecobee thermostats need steady power from the system. A calibrating message for up to about 20 minutes after power returns is normal. If it keeps restarting, that’s a power problem for a pro.

HW-FP6.text: Put in fresh AA alkaline batteries first.

HW-RTH76.text: Put in fresh AA alkaline batteries first.

HW-TH4.text: Put in fresh AA alkaline batteries first.

HW-X2P.text: Put in fresh AA alkaline batteries first.

AMZ-AST.text: The screen dims when idle. Touch the center button to wake it; gloves block the touch. This thermostat runs on power from the system.

HW-FP6.text: Replace Battery flashing means the batteries have about two months left. Put in fresh AA alkaline batteries. Swap them within about 2 minutes so the clock keeps its time.

NEST-NT.text: This model uses two AAA batteries. Pull the display straight off its base, put in fresh alkaline AAA batteries, and press it back on.

NEST-LT4.text: These models charge their battery from the system. A low-battery warning usually means they aren’t getting enough power, which a pro checks.

HW-T9.text: This model has no batteries to replace.

ECB-ESS.text: If the model has batteries you can reach without disconnecting wires, put in fresh alkaline batteries. If it has none, a pro checks power.

NEST-LT4.text: Nest shows help codes such as E1, E2, N260, or W5. W5 is Wi-Fi. E and N codes point to power or wire problems for a pro. In summer, E3, E4, E73, or E74 often mean the cooling shut itself off for a drain or safety reason.

HW-T9.text: Wi-Fi messages: NO INTERNET CONNECTION, WI-FI SIGNAL LOST. Room sensor: LOW SENSOR BATTERIES, INDOOR SENSOR CONNECTION ERROR. For a pro: HEAT PUMP FAILURE. The thermostat itself may need replacing: WIFI MODULE ERROR, MEMORY ERROR. POWER RESTORED is a notice.

ECB-PRM.text: Alerts are listed in the menu under reminders and alerts. Note the number. Heating or cooling problem alerts (1003 to 1006) are for a pro. 1009 and 1010 are about backup heat.

AMZ-AST.text: Status light: flashing red means a sensor, memory, clock, setup, or Wi-Fi fault, or a heat pump failure; the Alexa app shows which. Flashing yellow can mean emergency or backup heat, or the protection wait. A colored Info symbol on the screen means there’s a notice in the Alexa app.
